question: How often is the Master Circular on Health Insurance Business reviewed?
answer: The Master Circular shall be reviewed every year unless review or repeal is warranted earlier.
facts: The Master Circular shall be reviewed every year unless review or repeal is warranted earlier.

question: Who has the authority to issue clarifications to remove doubts or difficulties in the application of the Master Circular?
answer: The Competent Authority may issue appropriate clarifications as and when deemed necessary.
facts: In Order to remove any doubts or difficulties that may arise in the application or interpretation or any of the provisions of this Master Circular, the Competent Authority may issue appropriate clarifications, as and when deemed necessary.

question: If my health insurance policy is being revised under the new IRDAI regulations, who must approve the changes and how will my existing benefits be handled?
answer: The Product Management Committee (PMC) must approve the changes, and any benefits such as waiting period or moratorium period accrued to you will be protected and carried forward to the new policy.
facts: Revision in terms and conditions of the products that are warranted exclusively due to the application of any of the updated provisions contained in this circular or the IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations,2024 shall be carried out under the extant UIN, with the approval of Product Management Committee(PMC).
The PMC shall ensure that the benefits such as waiting period, Moratorium period accrued to the credit of the policyholder are protected and carried forward to the new policy issued.

question: Can an insurer extend benefits from the revised regulatory framework to existing policyholders?
answer: Yes, the insurer may extend the benefits arising out of the revised regulatory framework to existing policyholders.
facts: The Insurer may extend the benefits arising out of the revised regulatory framework to the existing policyholders.

question: Can an insurer offer a new rider that covers both Allopathy and AYUSH treatments for a policyholder with a pre‑existing chronic condition?
answer: Yes, insurers must provide products/add‑ons/riders that cover all types of existing medical conditions, including pre‑existing diseases and chronic conditions, and all systems of medicine such as Allopathy and AYUSH.
facts: pre-existing diseases and chronic conditions
all systems of medicine and treatments including Allopathy, AYUSH and other systems of medicine

question: Is a policyholder allowed to receive coverage for home‑care treatment in an emergency?
answer: Yes, policyholders shall not be denied coverage in case of emergency situations, including home‑care treatment.
facts: every situation of treatment including domiciliary hospitalization, outpatient treatment (OPD), Day Care and Homecare treatment
Policyholder shall not be denied coverage in case of emergency situations

question: Can I customize my health insurance policy with add-ons or riders based on my medical needs?
answer: Yes, insurers must allow customers to customize their products by choosing add-ons or riders that suit their medical conditions or specific needs.
facts: Insurers shall allow for customization of products by customer by providing the flexibility to choose products/add-ons/riders as per his/her medical conditions/specific needs

question: Will my insurer cover advanced treatments such as immunotherapy monoclonal antibody injections?
answer: Yes, insurers are required to cover technological advancements and treatments, including immunotherapy monoclonal antibody injections.
facts: Products are available to cover Technological Advancements & Treatments: Insurers shall endeavour to cover Technological Advancements and Treatments in their products.
Immunotherapy- Monoclonal Antibody to be given as injection

question: Which advanced medical treatments are covered under the health insurance policy as per the IRDAI circular?
answer: The policy covers Uterine Artery Embolization, HIFU, Balloon Sinuplasty, Deep Brain stimulation, Oral chemotherapy, Immunotherapy‑Monoclonal Antibody injection, Intra‑vitreal injections, Robotic surgeries, Stereotactic radio surgeries, Bronchial Thermoplasty, Vaporisation of the prostate (Green laser or holmium laser), IONM (Intra‑Operative Neuro Monitoring), Hematopoietic stem cell therapy for bone marrow transplant, and any other advanced technology treatment as per the product design.
facts: Uterine Artery Embolization
Deep Brain stimulation
Immunotherapy- Monoclonal Antibody to be given as injection
Intra vitreal injections
Stereotactic radio surgeries
Vaporisation of the prostrate (Green laser treatment or holmium laser treatment)
IONM - (Intra Operative Neuro Monitoring)
Stem cell therapy: Hematopoietic stem cells for bone marrow transplant for haematological conditions to be covered
Any other treatment using advanced technology, as per the product design

question: What types of immunotherapy are included in the coverage list?
answer: Immunotherapy covered is the Monoclonal Antibody to be given as injection.
facts: Immunotherapy- Monoclonal Antibody to be given as injection

question: Which laws must insurers comply with when offering health insurance products?
answer: Insurers must offer products in accordance with the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017; the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016; the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021; the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019; and the HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017.
facts: Insurers shall offer products in accordance with relevant provisions of the following Laws: a) The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017; b) The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016; c) The Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021; d) The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, and e) The HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017

question: What information must be provided with every health insurance policy?
answer: Every policy must be accompanied by a Customer Information Sheet (CIS) that explains the basic features of the policy in simple words.
facts: Customer Information Sheet (CIS): CIS is to be provided with every policy in the format as given in Annexure 1. It is a document provided by the Insurer along with the policy document that explains in simple words, basic features of a policy at one place.

question: Who must receive the CIS document when a new health insurance policy is issued?
answer: Every policyholder, whether an individual or a member of a group insurance policy, must receive the CIS document.
facts: be provided to every policyholder in case of both Individual Insurance policy holder as well as a Member of Group Insurance Policy
It is a document provided by the Insurer along with the policy document

question: What key information must the CIS include about claim handling and grievance redressal?
answer: The CIS must contain information regarding the Claims Procedure, Policy Servicing and Grievance Redressal Mechanism, including contact details of the Insurance Ombudsman.
facts: contain information regarding the Claims Procedure, Policy Servicing and Grievance Redressal Mechanism including contact details of Insurance Ombudsman

question: How long does a policyholder have to review a health insurance policy before deciding to cancel it?
answer: The policyholder has a 30‑day free look period from the date of receipt of the policy document.
facts: Free Look Period: A period of 30 days (from the date of receipt of the policy document) is available to the policyholder to review the terms and conditions of the policy

question: What notice period must a policyholder give to cancel a health insurance policy during its term?
answer: The policyholder must give a 7‑day written notice to cancel the policy.
facts: Cancellation of indemnity based health insurance policy by the policyholder: The policyholder may cancel his/her policy at any time during the term, by giving 7 days notice in writing

question: If I want to cancel my health insurance policy before it expires, how much notice do I need to give and what refund will I receive if my policy is less than a year old and I have not made any claims?
answer: You must give 7 days written notice. If the policy term is up to one year and no claims have been made, you will receive a refund of the proportionate premium for the unexpired period.
facts: "The policyholder may cancel his/her policy at any time during the term, by giving 7 days notice in writing."
"refund proportionate premium for unexpired policy period, if the term of policy upto one year and there is no claim (s) made during the policy period."

question: Can I change my nominee at any time during the policy term?
answer: Yes, you can change your nominee at any time during the term of the policy.
facts: "Nomination can be changed any time during the term of the policy."

question: If I want to change my nominee after the policy has started, how can I do it and is there any fee for the change?
answer: You can change your nominee at any time during the policy term. The insurer must provide a simple and seamless procedure for registering the change. No fee is mentioned for the change.
facts: Nomination can be changed any time during the term of the policy
Insurer shall put in place a simple and seamless procedure for registering and change in nomination in the policy

question: What happens if I miss my monthly premium payment by 10 days?
answer: You have a grace period of fifteen days for monthly instalments. If you pay within that period, the policy is renewed and all credits such as sum insured, No Claim Bonus, and waiting periods are protected.
facts: Grace period of fifteen days (where premium is paid on a monthly instalments)

If the policy is renewed during grace period, all the credits (sum insured, No Claim Bonus, Specific Waiting periods, waiting periods for pre-existing diseases, Moratorium period etc.) accrued under the policy shall be protected

question: If I pay my health insurance premium in instalments, will I still have coverage during the grace period?
answer: Yes, coverage will be available for the grace period as well.
facts: If the premium is paid in instalments during the policy period, coverage will be available for the grace period also

question: Can an insurer refuse to renew my health insurance policy simply because I have made a claim in previous years?
answer: No, an insurer cannot deny renewal on the basis of prior claims.
facts: An Insurer shall not deny the renewal on the ground that the policyholder had made a claim (s) in the preceding policy years

question: If a policyholder requests an increase in sum insured, can the insurer require fresh underwriting for the entire policy?
answer: No, the insurer may underwrite only to the extent of the increased sum insured and must not resort to fresh underwriting unless there is an increase in sum insured.
facts: An Insurer shall not resort to fresh underwriting unless there is an increase in sum insured
In case increase in sum insured is requested by the policyholder, the Insurer may underwrite only to the extent of increased sum insured

question: How long does the existing insurer have to provide underwriting details and claim history to the acquiring insurer after receiving a request via the Insurance Information Bureau of India portal?
answer: The existing insurer must provide the requested information within 72 hours of receiving the request.
facts: the existing insurer shall provide the information sought by the Acquiring insurer immediately but not more than 72 hours of receipt of request through Insurance Information Bureau of India (IIB)

question: Within what time frame must the acquiring insurer decide and communicate its proposal after receiving information from the existing insurer?
answer: The acquiring insurer must decide and communicate its proposal within 5 days of receiving the information.
facts: The Acquiring insurer shall decide and communicate on the proposal immediately but not more than 5 days of receipt of information from Existing insurer

question: If I have a health insurance policy with a previous insurer, can I transfer my No Claim Bonus to a new insurer when I switch plans?
answer: Yes, the policyholder is entitled to transfer the credits gained to the extent of the Sum Insured, No Claim Bonus, specific waiting periods, waiting period for pre-existing disease, Moratorium period, etc from the Existing Insurer to the Acquiring Insurer.
facts: policyholder is entitled to transfer the credits gained to the extent of the Sum Insured, No Claim Bonus, specific waiting periods, waiting period for pre-existing disease , Moratorium period etc from the Existing Insurer to the Acquiring Insurer

question: After how many months of continuous coverage can a health insurance policy or claim be contested for non-disclosure or misrepresentation?
answer: A policy or claim cannot be contested for non-disclosure or misrepresentation after the completion of the Moratorium Period, i.e., 60 months of continuous coverage.
facts: Policy/Claim cannot be contested: No policy and claim of health insurance shall be contestable on any grounds of non-disclosure and/or misrepresentation except for established fraud, after the completion of the Moratorium Period, i.e. 60 months of continuous coverage

question: What are the options for a policyholder to receive a No Claim Bonus at renewal?
answer: The policyholder can choose either a cumulative bonus, which adds to the sum insured without raising the premium, or a discount on the renewal premium.
facts: No Claim Bonus: The Insurer may reward the policyholders who do not make claim in the form of No Claim Bonus (NCB).

Such NCB shall be paid as per the choice/ express consent of the policyholder in the following forms at the time of every renewal: a) Cumulative Bonus: Addition in the Sum Insured without an associated increase in premium. and/or b) Discount in renewal Premium

question: What is the insurer’s target for cashless claim settlement?
answer: The insurer must aim for 100% cashless claim settlement within a time‑bound manner, minimizing reimbursement claims to only exceptional circumstances.
facts: Approval for Cashless facility: a. Every insurer shall strive to achieve 100% cashless claim settlement in a time bound manner. The insurers shall endeavor to ensure that the instances of claims being settled through reimbursement are at bare minimum and only in exceptional circumstances.

question: Within how many hours must an insurer decide on a cashless authorization request after receiving it?
answer: The insurer must decide on the request for cashless authorization immediately but not more than one hour of receipt of the request.
facts: "Insurer shall decide on the request for cashless authorization immediately but not more than one hour of receipt of request."

question: What is the maximum time allowed for an insurer to grant final authorization for a hospital discharge after receiving the discharge authorization request?
answer: The insurer must grant final authorization within three hours of the receipt of the discharge authorization request from the hospital.
facts: "Insurer shall grant final authorization within three hours of the receipt of discharge authorization request from the hospital."

question: If a hospital charges additional amounts due to a delay beyond the insurer’s three‑hour window, who pays those extra charges?
answer: The insurer must bear any additional amount charged by the hospital from its shareholder’s fund.
facts: delay beyond three hours
additional amount if any charged by the hospital
borne by the insurer from shareholder’s fund

question: If a hospital charges an additional amount after a delay of more than three hours, who is responsible for paying that amount?
answer: The insurer must bear any additional amount charged by the hospital beyond the three‑hour delay, using its shareholder’s fund.
facts: "If there is any delay beyond three hours, the additional amount if any charged by the hospital shall be borne by the insurer from shareholder’s fund."

question: What steps must an insurer take if a policyholder dies during treatment?
answer: The insurer must immediately process the claim settlement request and arrange for the mortal remains to be released from the hospital immediately.
facts: "In the event of the death of the policyholder during the treatment, the insurer shall: i. immediately process the request for claim settlement. ii. get the mortal remains (dead body) released from the hospital immediately"

question: If I have multiple indemnity health insurance policies and my claim exceeds the coverage of the chosen policy, what will the insurer do to settle the remaining amount?
answer: The insurer of the chosen policy will act as the primary insurer and will seek details of my other policies to coordinate with the other insurers to settle the balance amount, ensuring no hassle to me.
facts: The Insurer of that chosen policy shall be treated as the primary Insurer

In case the available coverage under the said policy is less than the admissible claim amount, the primary Insurer shall seek the details of other available policies of the policyholder and shall coordinate with other Insurers to ensure settlement of the balance amount

question: Can I claim from all insurers simultaneously if I have multiple benefit‑based health insurance policies and an insured event occurs?
answer: Yes, on occurrence of the insured event, I can claim from all insurers under all benefit‑based policies.
facts: Benefit based Policies: On occurrence of the insured event, the policyholders can claim from all Insurers under all policies

question: What must an insurer include in its response letter to a grievance?
answer: It must include the contact details of the concerned insurance ombudsman so the complaint can be escalated if the policyholder is not satisfied.
facts: contact details of concerned insurance ombudsmen
complaint can be escalated

question: How long does an insurer have to comply with an Insurance Ombudsman award and what penalty applies if it fails to do so?
answer: The insurer must comply within 30 days of receiving the award, and if it does not honour the award it must pay Rs. 5000 per day to the complainant, plus penal interest.
facts: within 30 days of receipt of award
penalty of Rs. 5000/- per day

question: What penalty amount is payable to a complainant for non‑compliance with the IRDAI regulations?
answer: A penalty of ₹5,000 per day shall be payable to the complainant.
facts: 5000/- per day shall be payable to the complainant
Such penalty is in addition to the penal interest liable to be paid by the Insurer

question: Which paragraph numbers will be detailed in the upcoming Master Circular under the IRDAI Regulations 2024?
answer: Paras 4, 5, 7, 12, 17, 18, 19 and 20 will be detailed in the forthcoming Master Circular.
facts: paras 4,5,7,12,17,18,19 and 20 above will be given in the Master Circular

question: What type of treatment options must IRDAI-approved health insurers provide to policyholders according to the circular?
answer: Insurers must offer Ayush treatments alongside other treatments, giving policyholders the option to choose their preferred treatment.
facts: "ensure Ayush treatments at par with the other treatments"
"provide option to the policyholders to choose treatment of their choice"

question: What service coverage must be available for all categories of hospitals under the IRDAI circular?
answer: Insurers must provide 100% cashless services for all categories of hospitals, covering domiciliary hospitalization, outpatient treatment (OPD), Day Care and Homecare treatment.
facts: "striving to provide 100% cashless services to the policyholders"
"for every situation of treatment including domiciliary hospitalization, outpatient treatment (OPD), Day Care and Homecare treatment"

question: What must insurers do regarding proposal forms and customer information sheets?
answer: Insurers must design proposal forms in simple language, provide them in scheduled languages, disseminate product information transparently, forward the CIS in the specified format, and obtain acknowledgement from the policyholder.
facts: Design the proposal forms in simple language
may also provide the proposal form and policy document in the scheduled languages
Disseminate information about the products to the prospects and policyholders in a transparent manner
Insurers shall mandatorily forward CIS in the specified format and obtain acknowledgement of the policyholder

question: What are the requirements for claims handling and settlement processes?
answer: Insurers must have well‑defined claims handling and settlement procedures, set turnaround times for settlement and policy servicing, and constitute a Claims Review Committee.
facts: Have in place well defined claims handling, claim settlement procedures, turnaround times (TATs) for settlement of claims and policy servicing
Constitute a Claims Review Committee (CRC)

question: Which committee must independently decide on the repudiation of every claim in a health insurance policy?
answer: The Claims Review Committee (CRC) must independently take the final decision on repudiation of every claim.
facts: Constitute a Claims Review Committee (CRC)

question: What information must insurers display prominently on their website regarding hospitals for cashless claim settlement?
answer: Insurers must display a list of hospitals or healthcare service providers with whom they have tie‑ups for cashless claim settlement and those in the common network list, and indicate that claims filed for other hospitals must be submitted for reimbursement.
facts: Display the following prominently on their website: a. List of the following i. hospitals/healthcare service providers with whom they have tie up for cashless claim settlement ii. hospitals/healthcare service providers which are in the list of common network of hospitals

question: What must an insurer do to ensure cashless claim settlement from the start of coverage for a group policy?
answer: The insurer must obtain the details of all members of the group from the master policyholder at the earliest, and no claim will be denied for lack of those details.
facts: Insurer shall obtain the details of members of the group from the master policyholder, at the earliest
No claim shall be denied for non-availability of details of members of the group

question: What are the steps insurers and insurance councils should take to provide a seamless cashless facility?
answer: They should establish common empanelment of hospitals so cashless service is available anywhere, and ensure a seamless journey for the policyholder at every point of sale, service and claim.
facts: Have in place common empanelment of hospitals/healthcare providers, so that cashless facility can be availed anywhere
Provide seamless journey to the policyholder at each point of sale, service and claim

question: What must insurers do to monitor the performance of their TPAs according to the IRDAI circular?
answer: Insurers must have board‑approved criteria for monitoring TPA performance, including customer servicing, turnaround times, and service level parameters.
facts: Insurers shall have Board approved criteria
servicing of the customers
TATs and service level parameters

question: Can the remuneration of a TPA be linked to the incurred claim ratio of the policies it serves?
answer: No, the remuneration of TPAs shall not depend on the incurred claim ratio of the policies they serve.
facts: In no case, the remuneration of TPAs shall depend upon the Incurred Claim Ratio (ICR) of the policies served by the TPAs

question: Who must be a member of the Product Management Committee as per the IRDAI circular?
answer: The Product Management Committee must include the Appointed Actuary, Chief Marketing/Distribution Officer, Chief Investment Officer, Chief Technology Officer, and Chief Compliance Officer of the insurer.
facts: "The PMC shall be constituted with Appointed Actuary (AA), Chief Marketing / Distribution Officer, Chief Investment Officer, Chief Technology Officer, and Chief Compliance Officer of the Insurer as members."

question: Under what condition must insurers pay TPAs according to the IRDAI circular?
answer: Insurers must pay TPAs only after the services have been availed and the TPA has fully discharged the services satisfactorily.
facts: "Insurers shall ensure that the payments are made to the TPAs only after availing the services and upon full discharge of services by the TPA satisfactorily."

question: Who must be a member of the Product Management Committee (PMC) as per the IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business?
answer: The PMC must include the Appointed Actuary, Chief Marketing/Distribution Officer, Chief Investment Officer, Chief Technology Officer, and Chief Compliance Officer of the insurer.
facts: The PMC shall be constituted with Appointed Actuary (AA), Chief Marketing / Distribution Officer, Chief Investment Officer, Chief Technology Officer, and Chief Compliance Officer of the Insurer as members.

question: What is the minimum quorum required for a PMC meeting, and how many members does it include?
answer: The quorum is three members in addition to the Appointed Actuary, making a total of four members required for a quorum.
facts: The quorum for the PMC shall be three members in addition to Appointed Actuary 5.

question: Who must countersign the certifications related to due diligence processes for an insurer's products?
answer: The CEO of the insurer must countersign the relevant certifications.
facts: The CEO of the Insurer shall have an overall responsibility for ensuring that a robust due diligence process is in place to mitigate risks arising from the products and shall countersign the relevant certifications.

question: What is the minimum composition of the Advertisement Committee for an insurer?
answer: The Advertisement Committee must include at least two Key Management Persons, three Senior Management Officials one level below the KMP, and a permanent invitee from the PMC of the insurer.
facts: The AC shall be constituted with a minimum of two Key Management Persons (KMP), three Senior Management Officials one level below the KMP and a permanent invitee from PMC of the Insurer (refer under 6(1)(c) of IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulation, 2024).

question: Which committee must approve a new health insurance product or rider before it can be launched?
answer: The Product Management Committee (PMC) of the insurer must approve it.
facts: Any new product or Rider or Add-on or modification of an existing Individual product or Rider or Add-on shall be approved by the Product Management Committee (PMC) of the Insurer.

question: What identification number must insurers obtain for each new health insurance product, and how is it obtained?
answer: Insurers must obtain a Unique Identification Number (UIN) by filing the proposed name and PMC approval date as per Annexure‑2.
facts: Insurers shall file the proposed name of the product, date of approval by PMC as per the Format at Annexure-2 and shall obtain the Unique Identification Number (UIN).

question: Which form must insurers use to maintain details of individual health products, riders, and add-ons?
answer: Insurers must use Form IRDAI‑HIP (Annexure‑3).
facts: Insurers shall maintain details of the (a) individual products /Riders/Add-Ons in the specified Form - IRDAI –HIP (Annexure - 3)

question: What is required before an insurer can modify an existing health product?
answer: The insurer must file an application in Form IRDAI‑HIP (Annexure‑3) with the PMC for approval.
facts: Modification of an existing product shall be approved by PMC. An Application as specified at Annexure 3 (Form - IRDAI –HIP) of this Circular shall be filed with PMC.

question: If an insurer fails to launch a modified product within 30 days from the date of generation of UIN, what must the insurer do?
answer: The insurer must undertake the process for obtaining approvals of the product or the modification afresh from the PMC.
facts: If an Insurer does not launch the product or modified product within a period of 30 days from the date of generation of UIN
the Insurer shall be required to undertake the process for obtaining approvals of the product or the modification afresh from the PMC

question: Within how many days must an insurer inform the PMC about the withdrawal of any product, add-on, or rider?
answer: The insurer must inform the PMC within 30 days from the date of withdrawal.
facts: Within 30 (thirty) days from the date of withdrawal
the same shall be informed vide Form IRDAI-HPW (Annexure – 5)

question: What must insurers do with a withdrawn individual health insurance product or add-on for existing customers?
answer: They must provide the existing customers with the options listed in the policy document for withdrawal of the product/add-on/rider.
facts: The Policy document shall clearly indicate the possibility of withdrawal of the product/add-on/rider in future and suitable options that would be made available to the policyholder on withdrawal of the products
A withdrawn Individual Health Insurance product/add-on/rider shall not be offered to new customers after the date of the withdrawal

question: If a health insurance product is withdrawn, how long do existing policyholders have to renew it before they must choose another option?
answer: Existing customers have a one‑time option to renew the product only if the renewal falls within 90 days from the date of withdrawal.
facts: A one‑time option to renew the existing product, if renewal falls within the 90 days from the date of withdrawal of the product

question: What must a Group Health Insurance Product’s PMC do if the product is withdrawn?
answer: The PMC must establish guidelines for withdrawal of the product.
facts: Provided in case of Group Health Insurance Product, the PMC shall put in place guidelines for withdrawal

question: Which groups must insurers provide a specific cover for under the IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business?
answer: Insurers must offer a specific cover for Persons with Disabilities (PWD), persons affected with HIV/AIDS, and those with mental illness.
facts: All general and health Insurers shall offer a specific cover for Persons with Disabilities (PWD), persons affected with HIV/AIDS, and those with mental illness

in compliance with the following provisions; I. Section 21(4) of The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017; II. Section 3 of The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016; and III. Section 3(j) of The HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017

question: What model product and documentation format must insurers follow when designing a health insurance product for PWD, HIV/AIDS, and mental illness?
answer: Insurers must use the model product as per Cir. No. IRDAI/HLT/CIR/MISC/58/2/2023 dated 27.02.2023 and the CIS must follow the format attached at Annexure 1.
facts: A model product setting out the minimum scope and parameters for design of the product is as per Cir. No. IRDAI/HLT/CIR/MISC/58/2/2023 dated 27.02.2023
and the CIS shall be as per the format attached at Annexure 1

question: When can a policyholder request a change in their sum insured, and what conditions apply to an increase in the sum insured?
answer: A policyholder can request a change in their sum insured only at the time of renewal or at any other time subject to underwriting by the company. For an increase, the waiting period starts afresh only for the enhanced portion of the sum insured.
facts: Sum Insured can be changed (increased/decreased) only at the time of renewal or at any time, subject to underwriting by the company.
For increase in SI, the waiting period if any shall start afresh only for the enhanced portion of the sum insured

question: What is the moratorium period for contestability of a health insurance policy, and when does it end?
answer: After five continuous years under the policy, no look‑back is applied; the moratorium period ends after five continuous years from the date of enhancement of the sum insured, after which the policy is not contestable except for fraud or permanent exclusions.
facts: After completion of Five continuous years under the policy no look back to be applied.
This period of Five years is called as moratorium period.

The moratorium would be applicable for the sums insured of the first policy and subsequently completion of Five continuous years would be applicable from date of enhancement of sums insured only on the enhanced limits.

question: What happens if a policyholder fails to disclose a pre‑existing disease before purchasing a health insurance policy?
answer: Non‑disclosure may affect the claim settlement.
facts: Please disclose all pre-existing disease/s or condition/s before buying a policy.
Non-disclosure may affect the claim settlement.

question: After the moratorium period, can a health insurance policy be contested for reasons other than fraud or permanent exclusions?
answer: No, it cannot be contested except for proven fraud and permanent exclusions specified in the policy contract.
facts: After the expiry of Moratorium Period no health insurance policy shall be contestable except for proven fraud and permanent exclusions specified in the policy contract.

question: How quickly must an insurer submit the required documents to IRDAI after a product modification request?
answer: Within two days of the request.
facts: within two days

question: Which form must an insurer file to introduce a new health insurance product or modify an existing one?
answer: An insurer must file the form IRDAI-HIP.
facts: An insurer, who wishes to introduce a new product/modification of existing product, shall file the form IRDAI-HIP annexed herewith.

question: How many separate forms are required for each new product and each add‑on or rider?
answer: A separate form must be filed for each product and for each add‑on or rider.
facts: A separate form shall be filed in respect of each such product and each such Add‑on or Rider.

question: If an insurer wants to offer Add‑on A with both Product X and Product Y, what financial documentation must they submit for each product?
answer: They must furnish separate financial projections and sensitivity analysis for Add‑on A with Product X and again for Add‑on A with Product Y, as the projections may differ under each product.
facts: financial projections for the Add‑on may differ under that product
financial projections / Sensitivity Analysis need to be furnished for the said Add‑on along with each product

question: Do insurers need to restate the Add‑on details when submitting financial projections for a second product?
answer: No, insurers only need to submit the financial projections; the Add‑on details do not need to be repeated.
facts: Addon details need not be mentioned again
only the financial projections are to be filed

question: If an insurer offers the same add‑on with multiple health insurance products, do they need to restate the add‑on details in each application?
answer: No, the insurer only needs to file the financial projections for the add‑on; the add‑on details do not need to be restated for the second or third product.
facts: "Addon details need not be mentioned again but only the financial projections are to be filed, when the same Add‑on is offered along with the second or the third product."

question: Who is required to initial every page of the IRDAI‑HIP application form?
answer: The appointed actuary must initial all pages of the application form.
facts: "The Appointed Actuary shall initial on all the pages of the IRDAI‑HIP application form."

question: What must insurers do regarding the brand name of a health insurance product after it is launched in the market?
answer: Insurers must not alter or modify the brand name in any form after launch, and the name must appear in all returns submitted to IRDAI.
facts: This name should not be altered / modified in any form after launching in the market.
This name shall appear in all returns etc. which would be submitted to IRDAI.

question: If an insurer wants to modify an existing health insurance product, what information must they provide regarding the modification?
answer: They must specify the sections being modified, provide the unique ID number, state how many days they intend to launch the modified version after allotment of UIN, and indicate the type of modification, including pricing changes with benefit structure changes.
facts: Specify the Sections which are being modified
Unique ID no. (where application is for modification of an existing product)
Within how many days the Insurer intends to launch the modified version of the product after allotment of UIN
Type of Modification 1. Pricing with change in Benefit Structure
